stemMd: The European Court of Human Rights, which sits in Strasbourg, decides cases brought under the European Convention on Human Rights. Which organisation is the Court part of?

options.label: E
options.textMd: The Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe

explanationMd:
**What to notice first.** The word *European* in the Court's name tempts you towards the European Union, but Europe has more than one international organisation, and they have their own courts.

**The facts that settle it.** The Council of Europe was founded in 1949 and has its seat in Strasbourg. Its member states signed the European Convention on Human Rights in Rome in 1950; the Convention entered into force in 1953, and the European Court of Human Rights was set up in 1959 to enforce it. The Council of Europe is a separate and larger organisation than the EU: its members include countries outside the EU, such as the United Kingdom, Norway, Switzerland and Turkey.

**How to check it.** Match each organisation with its own court. The EU's court is the Court of Justice of the European Union, in Luxembourg, which applies EU law. The United Nations' principal court is the International Court of Justice, in The Hague, which hears disputes between states. Neither NATO nor the OSCE has a human-rights court. Beware also the similar names: the *Council of Europe* is not the *European Council*, which is an EU institution of heads of state or government.

distractorRationale.c: This is the name trap. The EU has its own court, the Court of Justice of the European Union in Luxembourg, and its own rights text, the Charter of Fundamental Rights. Strasbourg also hosts the European Parliament's plenary sessions, which adds to the confusion, but the Court of Human Rights belongs to the Council of Europe.
distractorRationale.a: The UN does have a principal court, but it is the International Court of Justice at The Hague, and it settles disputes between states; individuals cannot bring cases before it. The Strasbourg court applies a European treaty, not the UN Charter.
distractorRationale.d: NATO was also founded in 1949, the same year as the Council of Europe, which can blur the two. But NATO is a military alliance for collective defence; it has no court of human rights.
distractorRationale.e: The OSCE grew out of the 1975 Helsinki Final Act and works on security, conflict prevention and election monitoring. Human rights are part of its agenda, but the European Court of Human Rights is not one of its bodies.

accessibilityText: Question: the European Court of Human Rights, which sits in Strasbourg, decides cases brought under the European Convention on Human Rights; which organisation is the Court part of? The choices are the United Nations, the Council of Europe, the European Union, the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, and the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe.

provenance.notes: Original item written for this bank for the TIL-A History and general knowledge section. The central misconception is attributing the Strasbourg court to the EU; the other distractors are international organisations with their own courts or none.

review.author: wave6-polito-til-a-genknow-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: The ECtHR is the Council of Europe's court under the ECHR. The EU's court is the CJEU in Luxembourg, so C is the classic confusion but it is wrong. The UN, NATO and the OSCE are not related. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave7-tila-reading-gk-run1) reached the same answer: The ECtHR is the court of the Council of Europe under the ECHR. The EU is the classic confusion, but the EU's court is the CJEU in Luxembourg. The UN, NATO and the OSCE are wrong.]

review.notes: Author's uniqueness check: the European Court of Human Rights is the Council of Europe's court (Council founded 1949; Convention signed 1950, in force 1953; Court set up 1959). It is not an organ of the EU, the UN, NATO or the OSCE. Awaiting a blind independent solve before publication.
